summary.en: Choose scatter, line and histogram views, label their units and read patterns without inventing causes.
summary.bn: scatter, line আর histogram বেছে নাও, একক লেখো আর কারণ ধরে না নিয়ে ছবির ধরন বোঝো।

notes: Python syntax works on 3.10+; Python 3.12 is recommended.
Use NumPy 2.0+, pandas 2.2+, scikit-learn 1.5+ and Matplotlib 3.8+ on a compatible Python.

sections.title: Draw one mark with a clear meaning
Avoid pictures that imply the wrong story
A plot is an argument you can inspect

examples.title: Colour the course fruits by label
examples.explanationHtml: Each point is one row of the shared fruit table. Different shapes and the legend identify labels without relying on colour alone. Nearby dots have similar plotted measurements, not necessarily identical labels.

examples.title: Connect observations that have an order
examples.explanationHtml: Completed overs have a natural order, so connecting neighbouring observations is meaningful. The line does not say exactly when within an over each run was scored.

examples.title: Count sizes inside histogram intervals
examples.explanationHtml: The intervals contain 1, 2 and 3 fruits. NumPy and Matplotlib include the final right endpoint, so size 9 belongs in the last interval. Histogram bars show counts over number ranges.

practice.title: Compute histogram counts
practice.statementHtml: Read 1–20 integer sizes in the inclusive range 0–9. For bins [0,3), [3,6), [6,9], print the three counts as a Python list.
hints: np.histogram uses a closed final interval.

practice.title: Save the requested numeric view
practice.statementHtml: Read scatter or line. For sizes [2,3,4,6,7] and sweetness [3,2,3,7,8], draw that view, label both axes, save view.png and print Saved view.png (K). A line connects the given order; it is an illustration rather than a recommended plot for unordered fruit records.
hints: Set Agg before importing pyplot and close the figure after saving.

practice.title: Select a useful picture
practice.statementHtml: Choose a plot for size versus sweetness, daily rainfall over a week, and the distribution of 120 fruit weights. Explain what a dot, line segment or bar represents.
hints: Ask whether the question concerns two measurements, sequence or frequency.
practice.answerHtml: Use scatter for paired fruit measurements: one dot per fruit. Use a line for rainfall in date order: the segment connects consecutive days but does not measure between-day rainfall. Use a histogram for weight frequency: a bar counts weights inside an interval. Label units and explain whether rainfall is daily or cumulative.

practice.title: Investigate an isolated dot
practice.statementHtml: A scatter plot shows one shopper with far higher spending than all others. Give two possible reasons and a next step.
hints: A point can be unusual without being a recording error.
practice.answerHtml: A misplaced decimal or a different spending unit may be an error. A large special purchase may be valid. Inspect the source row, units and collection context before deleting it. Preserve the original values and document any correction. The invented shop dataset includes such a case for investigation.

quiz.prompt: In the six-fruit scatter picture, which point should prompt a closer look?
options: p6 at size 9 and sweetness 1
p1 because every apple is an error
p4 because mangoes cannot be plotted
No point can ever be unusual
quiz.explanation: p6 is large but has much lower sweetness than the other mangoes. It may be valid or mistaken; the plot alone cannot decide.

caption.en: Six invented fruits; the rightmost mango is unlike the other mangoes.
caption.bn: ছয়টি বানানো ফল; সবচেয়ে ডানের আমটি অন্য আমগুলোর চেয়ে আলাদা।

quiz.prompt: Read the cricket line. How many runs were added during over 5?
quiz.explanation: The total rose from 15 after over 4 to 22 after over 5. The difference is 7, not the cumulative total 22.

caption.en: Team total after each of six ordered overs.
caption.bn: ছয়টি over শেষে দলের মোট রান।

quiz.prompt: In the histogram picture, how many fruits have size at least 6?
quiz.explanation: The final interval [6,9] contains sizes 6, 7 and 9. Its bar height is three.

caption.en: Counts in equal-width size bins; the final bin includes 9.
caption.bn: সমান চওড়া আকারের ঘরে সংখ্যা; শেষ ঘরে ৯-ও আছে।

quiz.prompt: Which plot suits the relationship between two measurements on unordered fruits?
options: A line connecting arbitrary file order
A histogram of row indices
An unlabeled total
A scatter plot
quiz.explanation: A scatter plot places one paired observation at each dot. Connecting unordered records suggests a sequence that the data does not contain.

quiz.prompt: Why include both units and a legend in a fruit plot?
options: Readers need the measurement scales and label meanings
They increase the number of observations
They prove a causal relationship
They remove every overlap
quiz.explanation: Axis units explain numbers and the legend explains colours or markers. Neither changes the measurements.

options: The complete Python environment
The figure as a file in the chosen format
Every notebook variable
A fitted classifier by default
quiz.explanation: savefig writes an image such as PNG. Preserve the code and data separately if you want to reproduce the picture.

quiz.prompt: Which statement about a rising size-weight cloud is supported by its picture alone?
options: Changing size must cause a specific weight
Every fruit follows a perfect rule
Larger plotted sizes tend to accompany larger plotted weights in these rows
The sample represents all fruit markets
quiz.explanation: A visible association is descriptive. Causation and generalisation require evidence beyond a scatter plot.

quiz.prompt: How many dots does this paired scatter input supply?
quiz.explanation: Five paired measurements supply five plotted points. There are two values per point.

quiz.prompt: Which histogram counts include the rightmost endpoint correctly?
quiz.explanation: The intervals hold [0], [3] and [6,9]. The final right endpoint is included.
quiz.code:
import numpy as np
counts, edges = np.histogram([0, 3, 6, 9], bins=[0, 3, 6, 9])
print(counts.tolist())

quiz.prompt: What change in cumulative runs would a line segment from over 3 to over 4 show?
quiz.explanation: The segment rises from 13 to 15, a difference of two runs.

keyPoints.en: A scatter point represents one pair of measurements.
keyPoints.bn: scatter-এর একটি বিন্দু দুটি মাপের একটি জোড়া বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: A line needs a meaningful order between observations.
keyPoints.bn: line আঁকতে পর্যবেক্ষণগুলোর অর্থপূর্ণ ক্রম থাকা দরকার।

keyPoints.en: A histogram counts measurements inside numeric intervals.
keyPoints.bn: histogram সংখ্যার নির্দিষ্ট ব্যবধানে মাপগুলো গোনে।

keyPoints.en: Axis units and legends explain how to read a figure.
keyPoints.bn: অক্ষের একক আর legend ছবি পড়ার অর্থ বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: Save and close figures when running noninteractive scripts.
keyPoints.bn: window ছাড়া script চালালে ছবি save করে figure বন্ধ করো।

keyPoints.en: A visible association alone cannot establish a cause.
keyPoints.bn: ছবিতে সম্পর্ক দেখা গেলেই কারণ প্রমাণ হয় না।

examQuestions.question: For sizes [2,3,4,6,7,9] and edges [0,3,6,9], list every bin and its count.
examQuestions.answerHtml: [0,3) contains 2, count 1. [3,6) contains 3 and 4, count 2. The final [6,9] contains 6, 7 and 9, count 3. Counts sum to six, the number of measurements. All bins have width three, so comparing heights compares counts fairly.

examQuestions.question: Specify an accessible scatter plot of fruit size and weight grouped by label.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Put size in centimetres on the horizontal axis and weight in grams on the vertical axis. Draw one group per label with both a different marker and a distinct colour. Add a legend naming the groups, a descriptive title and some transparency for overlaps. Save the figure at readable resolution. State that these are invented measurements.

examQuestions.question: Explain why a positive trend between two plotted measurements does not establish causation.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A rising pattern says larger values tend to occur together in these observations. Another variable, selection rules or measurement choices could produce that pattern. A plot alone does not distinguish these explanations. For the course’s fictional datasets, the relationships were chosen by the author rather than discovered in the world.
